verification.observed: Layer contract test: 73 passed. grep count: 3. Ladder: with SM_SCRIPTS_DIR set to the source scripts dir it printed that dir (exit 0). With CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=plugins/src/base and no SM_SCRIPTS_DIR it printed <root>/skills/lisa-session-manager/scripts (exit 0). With SM_SCRIPTS_DIR=/nonexistent it fell through: rung 3 resolved the installed lisa@lisa 4.33.1 cache dir (it has no session-manager yet), rung 4 had no npm copy, and it printed 'lisa-session-manager scripts not found' (exit 1). The relative paths $SM/../../../scripts/resolve-lifecycle-role.mjs and $SM/../references/runbook-template.md both resolve in the source tree.

deviations: The ladder improves on design section 2.3 in one way: rung 3 runs when rung 1 or 2 is set but its session-manager.mjs is missing, not only when SM is empty. That is the design's own risk-4 mitigation (a Lisa upgrade deletes the old plugin cache dir under a running manager), enforced in the snippet instead of described in prose.
The ladder ends with echo "$SM". Claude Code's Bash tool does not keep shell variables between calls, so the skill says to resolve once per cycle and use the printed absolute path.

Untrusted text (Telegram messages, worker messages, questions, reasons, summaries) is written with the Write tool to .lisa/session-manager/msg.txt and redirected into STDIN. It never goes on a command line. The CLI already reads only STDIN for this text; this closes the shell-quoting gap at the skill side.

Root check at the start of each cycle: `validate --project-root "$PWD"` must exit 0. A child repo's .lisa.config.json has no sessionManager block, so validate exits 2 there. That makes the design's risk-5 pwd check a CLI call.

The role resolver is reached as $SM/../../../scripts/resolve-lifecycle-role.mjs (the plugin root), not the ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-plugins/lisa} form other skills use, because that fallback is wrong in a host project.
When several outcome rows apply in one cycle, the skill picks the most urgent: recovery-required, then approval-requested, then change-proved. Design section 8 did not say how to break a tie.

Stalled or dead items that a human moved out of the claimed role are retired from the ledger with `ledger finish --status FAILED` and are not moved on the tracker. This follows the rule against retrying a human reversal (#3756). The CLI has no neutral 'untracked' finish status.
The skill has no allowed-tools. The manager runs with bypass permissions, and the Telegram reply tool is a plugin MCP tool whose name the skill cannot portably pin.

learnings.note: In Claude Code's Bash tool, shell variables do not persist between calls but the cwd does. A skill that resolves a path into a variable (like $SM) must either re-run the resolver in every call or print the path and have the agent substitute it. A cd in one call does carry into the next, so a claim-in-child-cwd step must always cd back.
learnings.evidence: The Bash tool contract in this session ('Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist'); design section 10 risk 5

learnings.note: The parity-safety-net hook refuses `bash $VAR/script.sh` even when the file exists: it needs a literal path to classify the script. Run extracted scripts by their full literal path.
